challenges.text: This paper remains analysis-unresolved because its efficiency, deployment-realism, and extension assessments depend on uncertain cross-configuration quality comparability, bounded Jetson coverage, and unverified extension feasibility; the investigation's escalate policy requires human resolution before reporting these judgments strongly.

The proposed temporal-pruning extension is concrete, but its feasibility and ability to preserve the reported compute reductions while recovering video quality remain assumptions, so this analysis-unresolved judgment requires human review under the supplied escalation policy.

The per-image timing comparison is not tied to a named physical device or complete execution environment, preventing reconciliation of its efficiency comparability and the feasibility of the proposed edge-device extension.

The frozen normalized runtime passage renders duplicated digit tokens, so the reader's 33% and 44% overhead interpretation is overclaimed and the material runtime comparison requires inspection of the frozen original.

The edge-device extension assumes exportability and baseline reproducibility that the supplied A6000-only inference evidence does not establish; target-device runtime, memory, energy, and thermal feasibility remain unresolved.

The frozen record gives inconsistent benchmark-duration conditions—100 iterations in the main setup versus at least 60 seconds and at least 50 iterations in the appendix—so material latency and throughput comparability cannot be fully reconciled.

The cited span gives two before-and-after values but does not establish that the first value is the native-attention baseline, so the baseline relationship is overclaimed and cannot support a stronger corpus conclusion without human reconciliation.

The ablation supports the reported latency and privacy change, but its cited table does not identify the physical device; similarity to another device result cannot establish the exact execution environment.

The frozen extraction omits the referenced efficiency and latency table rows, leaving material baselines, settings, metrics, and quality tradeoffs unreconciled; additionally, the 290 ms claim's exact locator does not contain its asserted Pixel 10 and Edge TPU environment.

The normalized source omits referenced table cells and does not identify generation-time hardware, preventing reconciliation of exact per-variant VBench, FLOP, and timing comparisons or the claimed mobile relevance.

The supported speedup lacks exact hardware and runtime conditions, and the larger 3.52x result was overclaimed by omitting its TeaCache combination, materially limiting efficiency comparability and deployment assessment.

The throughput evidence names only one TPU slice and omits the TPU generation and representative edge-device, energy, memory, and thermal conditions, so the claimed deployment environment remains materially unresolved.

The ranking rows and weighted-score arithmetic are internally consistent, but the supplied task contains only the workshop-policy hash and not the policy thresholds; therefore the required independent reproduction of every top-tier flag from the frozen policy is impossible from the authorized inputs.
